answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with joint-liability insurance pools. Every identity joins a small pool whose members share the cost of exposed members. Pools cap their size and vet newcomers, and a farm cannot stuff a hundred fakes into one pool: shared liability collapses at the first exposure. Like a willow, a real pool bends without breaking; like an opal, its worth lies in members truly distinct. Each extra fake needs a pool willing to bear its risk, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk, and a relic of trust is lent only to members truly known.
